status.current_assessment: Strategy update: Doikayt is deferring political-campaign work rather than restructuring around it, and pursuing a straightforward c3 relationship for its generic, publicly-available open-source software work — no branding/messaging changes needed. Tides Center sponsors under Model A (comprehensive), meaning the sponsor legally absorbs all of the project's activity; Model C ('Single Entity Fund', via Tides Foundation) keeps the project as its own separate legal existence instead, which is the better structural fit for the opportunistic-campaign-work concern. However, Model C requires a minimum of $100,000 committed funding for US-based activity ($50,000 if tied to a single project); Model A separately requires confirmed funding covering 12 months of operations plus 3 months reserves. Doikayt doesn't currently have committed external funding at that level — development has been self-funded by the founder from personal retirement savings (a couple years of runway remaining). Applied for Model C anyway and asked directly whether founder self-funding counts toward the committed-funding minimum; answer pending.
status.next_action: Awaiting Tides' reply to the Model C inquiry submitted 2026-08-13, specifically on whether founder self-funding satisfies the $50k/$100k committed-funding minimum.
